description: A call that does not yield to the event loop (`time.sleep`, a sync HTTP client, heavy computation); every task waits until it returns.
Runs a blocking function in a worker thread and awaits its result (3.9); in Pyodide it runs synchronously because there are no threads.
The global interpreter lock of the default CPython build: one thread executes Python bytecode at a time, released during blocking I/O.
A CPython build without the GIL (PEP 703, `python3.14t`): officially supported but optional since 3.14 (PEP 779).
`ProcessPoolExecutor` runs functions in separate processes for CPU parallelism; arguments and results are pickled.
Isolated interpreters in one process, each with its own GIL: `concurrent.interpreters` and `InterpreterPoolExecutor` (3.14, PEP 734).
